faqs.q: How long does a tile roof last on an older Orange home?

runs.v: Clay tile can last a century or more, but the underlayment fails first, so a 30-to-50-year-old tile roof commonly needs underlayment renewal.

faqs.q: Can individual broken tiles on my Orange roof be replaced without re-covering the whole roof?

runs.v: Yes. Repairs involve replacing individual damaged tiles with matched ones and checking the underlayment, without disturbing the surrounding tiles.

faqs.q: Does tile roofing in an Orange historic district require special approval?

runs.v: It can: a property in a historic district can need extra review, so confirm with the City of Orange Township construction office before work begins.

faqs.q: Can my Orange house support the weight of a tile roof?

runs.v: A structural assessment answers it, and reinforcing the framing for the tile load needs a permit.

faqs.q: Do concrete tiles hold up to Orange freeze-thaw winters?

runs.v: Concrete tile carries a freeze-thaw spalling risk that proper ventilation and underlayment manage, while clay tile resists freeze-thaw well.

faqs.q: How much does tile roof installation and repair cost in Orange, NJ?

runs.v: Tile roof repair runs $500 to $2,500, per HomeGuide; NJ ranges sit 10 to 40% above national figures because of higher labor and stricter NJ code.

faqs.q: What is the 25% rule for roofing in New Jersey?

runs.v: It is a permit threshold under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7: on buildings other than detached one- and two-family homes, repairing up to 25% of the roof area in 12 months is ordinary maintenance. Beyond ordinary maintenance, roofing work in Orange requires a building permit under the NJ Uniform Construction Code.
